# Influence Psychology Skill for Muse

Curated by Skill Harbor — a free, open-source skill (MIT), listed here with credit to its creator @wondelai. Brings Cialdini's seven principles of ethical persuasion — reciprocity, commitment, social proof, authority, liking, scarcity, unity — into product and copy work: when each principle applies, how to use it in landing pages, testimonial sections, and trust signals, and where the ethical limits are. Honest notes: it improves how persuasively you present a real offer — it can't fix a weak product or manufacture trust you haven't earned; manipulative uses (fake scarcity, false social proof) are explicitly out of scope of the ethical framing; marketing advice, not legal compliance — dark patterns that violate consumer law stay your responsibility. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
